title: Exact Mayer--Vietoris segment for module-sheaf pullbacks
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $i:Z\to X$ a morphism of schemes, $J$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $X$, $U,V\subseteq X$ opens with $U\cup V=X$, and $r\in\mathbb N$. With the scheme and site conventions [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], let $F$ be the underlying abelian sheaf of $i^*J$, and $F_T$ the underlying abelian sheaf of $\operatorname{pr}_1^*(T.\iota^*J)$ on $T\times_XZ$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. There exist additive homomorphisms $\delta:H^r(F_{U\cap V})\to H^{r+1}(F)$ and $\rho:H^{r+1}(F)\to H^{r+1}(F_U)\times H^{r+1}(F_V)$ such that $\operatorname{im}\delta=\ker\rho$, where cohomology is Sheaf.H [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. No vanishing hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Two-open long exact sequence, transported via inverse-image composition and underlying abelian sheaves (Tags 03D3 and 03D7).

proof.text: Base change of each open inclusion is an open immersion; its image is the inverse-image open in Z. The two images cover Z, and the base change of U ∩ V identifies with their intersection. Identify each base-change scheme with its image.
Inverse-image composition and forgetting module structure identify the restrictions of the underlying abelian sheaf of i^*J with the displayed sheaves; transport across the scheme isomorphisms.

Apply etale_mayerVietoris to F on Z and its inverse-image open cover. Use nonempty_sheafH_extDerivedIso to pass from derived cohomology to Sheaf.H. Transport the connecting and restriction homomorphisms through the additive identifications of the four groups. These preserve images and kernels, yielding the exact pair without any vanishing assumptions.
